_comment: Human labels for ten incidents, scored against the same rubric the judge reads
(eval/judge/rubric.md). Ten rather than forty because the labelling is the
expensive part and a number backed by ten careful judgements is worth more than
one backed by forty rushed ones -- the honest limitation is stated in the report
rather than hidden by a larger n.
The judge scores here are the ones the judge role produced on the same drafts.
They are recorded rather than recomputed on every run: the judge is the one
component in this harness that is not deterministic, and re-running it inside
the gate would make the gate non-deterministic to report a number it does not
Read the disagreements, not the rate. Incident 233 is where a person and the
judge diverge on root-cause reasonableness: the draft abstains, a person scores
the abstention 2 because nobody established a cause, and the judge scores it 1
because it read 'no hypothesis' as 'incomplete'. That is a real and instructive
failure -- a judge that penalises honest uncertainty would train the prompt
towards confident invention, which is the exact failure this project exists to
